text:
gSASRec directly supports testing the objective bottleneck: keep SASRec’s architecture, increase negatives, replace BCE with generalized BCE. Its positive term is −β log σ(s+), with ordinary negative BCE terms; β=1−t+tα, α=k/(catalogue_size−1). Authors recommend k=256, t=0.75; t=1 targets full calibration but converges more slowly. Evidence originates in RecSys 2023, with a [2024 extended abstract](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf); the [author implementation](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec) documents these settings. This supports an objective ablation, without establishing gains on the four Amazon categories.

Sampled softmax is another strong candidate. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies a strong combination using SASRec’s next-item training task, LiGR layers and sampled softmax; its combined results do not isolate loss effects. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that conventional in-batch correction mishandles the always-present positive: importance correction must account for its deterministic inclusion. Popularity or mixed sampling therefore needs proposal-aware treatment; copying an in-batch correction onto uniform sampling is unjustified.

Sampling controls matter separately from loss. A [2024 comparative study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent accuracy/popularity tradeoffs; aggregate gains can conceal weaker tail performance. Proposed compute-conscious experiment: hold architecture fixed, compare multi-negative BCE, gBCE and sampled softmax at k=32/64, then expand promising settings toward 256. Exclude padding, target collisions and observed training positives; unobserved items can still be false negatives, so avoid assuming hard negatives are truly irrelevant. Select exclusively by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, recording GPU time. Electronics’ weak margins motivate this experiment but cannot establish generalization gains.
